Identity.History: Thebes was one of the foremost cities of Boeotia and a major power in classical Greece, often competing with Athens and Sparta. After throwing off Spartan domination in 379 BC, Thebes rose rapidly under Pelopidas and Epaminondas, crushing the Spartan army at Leuctra in 371 BC and briefly establishing Theban supremacy. Its influence declined after Epaminondas was killed at Mantinea in 362 BC. Alexander the Great destroyed Thebes in 335 BC, though the city was later rebuilt.
